newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL H1 NET INCOME UP DESPITE GAS LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: MOL H1 NET INCOME UP DESPITE GAS LOSSES.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt registered a 17.4 percent increase in group net income in the first half of 1997 from the same period of 1996, the company said in a statement on Thursday.
"Excluding the...3.84 billion forints cash receipt from (chemicals firm) TVK from the 1996 results, IAS net income shows a growth of 83.2 percent," the statmenet said.
MOL posted an IAS group net income of 12.545 billion forints in the first half of 1997 compared with 10.689 billion in the same period of 1996.
MOL's CEO Zoltan Mandoki said in the group's earnings report that the interim results were broadly in line with expectations.
However, MOL said that its gas business remained loss-making despite a 13.5 percent gas price increase in July.
"We remain committed to...achieve a more liberal natural gas pricing regime over the medium term," MOL said.
In the first half of 1997, MOL imported 65 percent of the gas and sold it at state-controlled prices with an average loss of five forints per cubic meter.
"The natural gas business suffered an estimated loss of 4.6 billion forints during the first half of 1997," MOL said.

It added, however, that the loss was not at the operating income level as it took into account 1.5 billion forints of allocated interest costs, 2.1 billion forints of inventory holding costs and 1.9 billion forints of allocated overhead costs.
The company said it had maintained or increased its market share in the two largest product groups during the first half of 1997.
"Wholesale market share in motor gasolines was up to 88 percent (from 80 percent in H1 1996) and for gas and heating oils was up to 91 percent (from 88 percent in H1 1996)," MOL said.
It added that after years of declining consumption, sales of motor gasolines rose five percent in volume terms in the first half of 1997.
"The Hungarian oil product market has shown the first signs of recovery after many years of contraction," Mandoki said in the report.
Motor gasoline sales rose to 672,000 tonnes in the first half of 1997 from 625,000 tonnes in the first half of 1996, MOL's figures showed.
However, fuel oil sales in the first half of 1997 dropped to 628,000 tonnes from 639,000 tonnes in the first half of 1996.
MOL said it had spent 31.7 billion forints on capital expenditures and investments in the first half of 1997.
MOL's figures showed that its end of June headcount was 14,118 compared with 15,786 in June 1996.
